boundaries.contract: engine_list_cleanup takes no caller arguments and returns no value. Two preconditions are owed to it and are stated in its own `# Safety` block at src/engine/eng_list.rs:130-158: (1) the engine lock is initialised (non-NULL), and (2) the calling thread does not already hold it, because this body takes it. With a NULL lock, lock() answers false and the cleanup returns with the list intact: a documented no-op and a leak, not undefined behaviour. The body takes the engine write lock first, loads ENGINE_LIST_HEAD under it, checks for null, calls engine_list_remove(head) under the same lock and unlocks after; no head value ever crosses an unlock, so no other thread can unlink the head or release its structural reference between the observation and the removal. The removal is engine_list_remove, the body ENGINE_remove runs while holding the same lock, at the same nesting depth, reaching the same engine_free_util.
precondition_set: the calling thread does not already hold the engine lock
established: src/engine/eng_list.rs:158-180 at S=15bebabc9 is the callback body: lock(); ENGINE_LIST_HEAD.load(Acquire); null check; engine_list_remove(head); unlock(). The load and the removal are inside one lock/unlock pair. The instrument's resolve_operation_span returns this span uniquely (resolution 'unique') for locators 158, 97 and no locator alike, at source commit S, sha256 f1103798b4ca53c49d85fe57b306f6d74d2c7444fbe3ec543086a9977ba7cfa4.

The same query at the repair commit 0d39697ae returns the same extent 158-180 and the same sha256 f1103798..., and src/engine/eng_list.rs hashes to 1e96f04c... at both commits: the frozen candidate contains exactly the repaired body.

The same query at b6f38f134 returns extent 97-111, sha256 5a8e4bab4b0840ff2a834a440d1144e68428765b616757620a25b4b3e663aafb, file sha256 76050c6d...; that is exactly the extent and hash r13-coordinate-rebind-sites.json records for the ledger key src/engine/eng_list.rs:97. The old record described the body that existed then; it is not wrong, it is stale.

src/engine/eng_list.rs:86-128 at S is the test-only observation point: mod cleanup_order_probe is #[cfg(test)] and no release build contains it. It records whether the engine write lock was held by the calling thread at every step.

src/engine/eng_list.rs:855-930 at S (fn at :856, span sha256 c780dcdc213fa52eafa61d85f3d2e478897673f4497bd0e60ad40a5d889ee72d, instrument-verified at both 0d39697ae and S) is tests::cleanup_observes_the_head_under_the_engine_lock.

The body of the test asserts cleanup_order_probe::steps() >= 1 and cleanup_order_probe::lock_was_held_at_every_step(), i.e. the head was observed and removed by a thread that already held the engine write lock.
The commit message of 0d39697ae records the mutation observation: restoring the pre-fix ordering (load the head outside the lock, then call ENGINE_remove) makes the canary fail with exit 101.
With a NULL lock the body returns with the list intact: lock() answers false, nothing is loaded, nothing is freed. That is a no-op/leak, not UB, and the contract states it.

caller_closure.registration: The only installation is engine_cleanup_add_last(Some(engine_list_cleanup)) at src/engine/eng_list.rs:237, in engine_list_add, and only on the transition of the list from empty to non-empty.
caller_closure.only_producer_of_a_list_member: ENGINE_add -> engine_list_add. Its engine came from ENGINE_new or ENGINE_by_id, both of which run the engine lock initialisation, so precondition (1) is established by the only path that can make the list non-empty.
caller_closure.invocation: OPENSSL_cleanup -> engine_cleanup_int -> engine_cleanup_cb_free(item) -> cb(). engine_cleanup_int is withheld in this candidate (src/engine/eng_lib.rs:697-704: 'engine_cleanup_int ... is withheld'), and engine_cleanup_cb_free is marked #[allow(dead_code)] at src/engine/eng_lib.rs:685 with that reason, so the callback is registered but unreachable at S. engine_cleanup_cb_free's own contract (src/engine/eng_lib.rs:676-685) states the engine lock must be initialised and must not be held by the thread that runs the item's callback; it takes no engine lock itself, so precondition (2) holds on the only invocation path.
caller_closure.no_safe_rust_caller: engine_list_cleanup is private, is not exported, takes no caller-supplied pointer, and no safe-Rust path registers or invokes it. Registration passes a private fn item; the runner that would invoke it is not landed.
caller_closure.lock_order: The only other lock reached under the engine lock is the ex_data registry mutex, which snapshots callbacks under it and drops it before invoking them: engine_lock -> ex_data_registry and never the reverse.

retained_obligations.why_retained: This is the authority's own ordering and the crate's pre-existing behaviour, not something the repair moved; deferring destruction past unlock would change destroy sequencing.
